name: Vostochny Site 1S
tagline: Russia's Soyuz-2 pad in the Far East: first launch 2016, OneWeb batches, Luna 25 (2023)
description: Site 1S is the Soyuz-2 launch pad at the Vostochny Cosmodrome in Amur Oblast, in Russia's Far East at 51.9 degrees north. Russia began building Vostochny in 2011, on the site of the former Svobodny missile base, so it could launch from its own territory instead of renting Baikonur from Kazakhstan. The first launch from 1S, a Soyuz-2.1a carrying the Mikhailo Lomonosov gamma-ray satellite, lifted off on 28 April 2016 at 02:01 UTC. The second, Meteor-M 2-1 in November 2017, was lost because the Fregat stage had been programmed for a Baikonur launch. Between December 2020 and October 2021, six Soyuz launches for Arianespace put 216 OneWeb satellites into orbit from here. On 10 August 2023 it launched Luna 25, which reached lunar orbit and then crashed on the Moon.
